quarterly_data.signal: Book-to-bill improved month by month through Q2 and reached 2.2 by end of June (from roughly 1.3-1.5 last quarter). Customers - mostly the high-growth AI-driven names in computing and enterprise whose programs involve memory/SSDs - are increasingly asking for long-term agreements and are even willing to pay a premium to secure passive-component supply for the next 6 months, a year, in some cases multi-year baselines; some have already placed orders under these talks. The conversations typically start with capacitors (across dielectrics, not just MLCC or tantalum) and extend across resistors, circuit protection, inductors and sensors. LTA interest currently comes mostly from direct end customers (fulfillment can still run through distribution/EMS), and management noted demand acceleration in certain areas - 'memory, solid state drive is a good example'.

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity is tight: Q3 utilization rates will be raised above 90% for BOTH commodity and specialty (from about 85% blended / 80% commodity in Q2) to meet demand and rebuild healthy inventory. Capacity is being expanded across the board - Kaohsiung (the large purpose-built MLCC fab, running tight), Vietnam, Suzhou and Mexico - led by tantalum and MLCC; only less than NT$3 billion of capex was spent in H1 with larger increments planned for H2, and equipment lead times are long so expansion is planned ahead, adding capacity quarter by quarter. Channel inventory is lean and healthier than a year ago: Greater China distribution about 2 months on hand (about five to six turns, versus 3 months a year ago), global distribution about 4 months, high-service channel 5-6 months (from 7-8 a year ago).

quarterly_data.signal: Management endorsed as 'a fair characterization' the view that high-capacitance MLCC demand ramping alongside next-generation AI servers will force conversion of mid/low-end capacity and put shortage pressure on the rest of the portfolio - part of its customer conversations already cover securing that non-AI piece too, with peers also raising MLCC utilization. Adjacent driver: the whole AI power chain 'from the grid down to the rack of the server' has many voltage step-down/conversion stages needing filtering and ripple-current management, driving strong growth in film capacitors and aluminum electrolytic capacitors plus the magnetics (inductors) and connector lines - embedded across computing, industrial and telecom segments. In notebooks, new tantalum packaging offering higher capacitance in a smaller package positions a laptop recovery as more of a 2027 story.
